capacity_checks.notes: 54 distinct given triples confirmed. But part (b) depends only on (r,s): 18 distinct (OA,OB) pairs and 14 distinct 1-dp angles; each (b) sub-question recurs verbatim in 3 instances. Part (a) has 30 distinct p values; 49 distinct (p,theta) pairs. A=C (r=t) in 18/54. p=0 in 6, right angle in 6, both (and A=C) in 2. Acute/right/obtuse = 30/6/18. Exact angles 60.0 (3 tuples) and 90.0 (6 tuples).

findings.expected: Accuracy rule for p matches the prompt and the NSSCAS default (syllabus PDF18/printed15 note 3: if accuracy not specified and answer not exact, 3 s.f.). Either the prompt asks for p exactly (and says terminating decimals such as 0.375 are accepted), or a:A1 accepts a correct 3 s.f. decimal.
findings.actual: a:A1 requires 'Correct exact p' but the prompt only asks for 'the scalar p'. 44/54 tuples have non-integer p; 13 are recurring (denominators 3, 6, 11, e.g. 5/11). A learner writing 0.455 per the syllabus default would lose A1. Also b:A1 '1 dp' must accept exact 60 deg (3 tuples) and 90 deg (6 tuples) without a trailing .0.
findings.evidence: Syllabus PDF18 notes 2-3 (rendered); enumeration: p denominators {1:10,2:7,3:7,4:8,5:10,6:1,8:6,11:5}.
findings.repair: Add 'Give p as an exact value' to the question (and accept exact terminating decimals), or accept 3 s.f.; state that exact angle values (60, 90) earn b:A1.

findings.locator: work/nam-8227-nsscas-2026/workbench/work-orders/WB8227-vector-geometry.md:13,16,32; planning/visual-design.json recipes[2] part a; planning/coverage-plan.md:71,73; PLAN.md:60
findings.expected: Part (a) direct demands include 8227:2020:M1:T7:O02:D01 'Add and subtract vectors' (syllabus PDF12 bullet 'perform addition and subtraction of vectors...'), because a:B1 is exactly the subtraction pOA-OB. D03 'Interpret geometric vector relation' is listed only if a criterion assesses a geometric interpretation of the operation.
findings.actual: Part (a) omits D01 and claims D03, which no a-criterion assesses (B1 components, M1 dot=0, A1 p; perpendicularity is O05:D02). The WO and PLAN describe D01 as 'addition' and use that as the reason to withhold the (a) same-type label; the accepted source part 2025 P1 Q3(a) maps {O02:D01, O02:D02, O04:D02, O05:D02}. coverage-plan lists D01 as later-syllabus-scope and D03 as a pilot-direct facet, so the 38/138 facet count rests on this error.
findings.evidence: demand-registry.json D01 learner_action 'Add and subtract vectors'; question-analysis.json 8227:EXAM:2025:P1:Q3:a; rendered syllabus PDF12.
findings.repair: Put D01 in part (a), drop D03 (or add a criterion that really assesses it), recompute coverage counts, and redo the part (a) equality check. With D01 in and D03 out the direct-demand set equals the source part's, so decide the (a) label on the response/givens/scaffold comparison rather than the mislabel.

findings.expected: Admitted instances name three distinct points A, B, C, and the boundary exemplar shows the p=0 and right-angle boundaries without collapsing parts (a) and (b) into one fact.
findings.actual: OA=(1,r,1) and OC=(1,t,1) coincide whenever r=t: 18/54 instances (33%) say 'position vectors of A, B and C' with A=C. In these, (a)'s OB.OC is (b)'s OA.OB, so part (a) hands part (b) its B1 value. In (2,-1,2) and (3,-2,3), p=0 and the right angle are the same fact (OB perpendicular to OA=OC). The 'admitted boundary' exemplar (3,-2,3) is one of these doubly collapsed cases.
findings.evidence: Enumeration: A==C 18; p=0 and theta=90 together only at (2,-1,2),(3,-2,3), both with A=C.
findings.repair: Exclude r=t (capacity 36) or change the OC template so OC is never equal to OA. Show the boundaries separately, e.g. p=0 at (1,-1,2) and a right angle at (2,-1,1).

findings.expected: Capacity and no-repeat keys reflect what the learner actually sees in each assessed part; per contract (recipe-contract.md:199-202) report finite capacity and repeated collisions honestly.
findings.actual: t does not enter part (b). Part (b), the only part with a learner same-type label, has 18 distinct (OA,OB) problems and 14 distinct 1-dp answers; each recurs verbatim across 3 of the '54 distinct' instances. The full-triple fingerprint treats these as fresh. The template is also rigid: 5 entries are fixed in every instance, |OA| and |OB| take only sqrt3, sqrt6 or sqrt11, and every angle lies in 58.5-121.5 deg. Numbers are easier than the source (components up to 6 with mixed signs), even though perpendicularity is a grade-a descriptor (PDF20).
findings.evidence: Enumeration of all 54 tuples; rendered syllabus PDF20.
findings.repair: Report part (b) capacity 18 alongside 54 and add part-level semantic keys, or make (b) depend on all parameters (for example by varying more slots or signs). Record calibration against the source magnitude.

findings.expected: Samples and feedback cover the examiner-evidenced (a) errors: 2025 report PDF346/printed344 marks Q3(a) 'Poorly answered', says most candidates stopped at p(OA)-(OB), and names the common wrong resultant p(OA-OB).
findings.actual: No sample covers p(OA-OB). Across the domain, p(OA-OB).OC = p(3-s+rt-t) = 0 gives the correct p=0 in all 6 admitted p=0 tuples (including the boundary exemplar) and an identity 0=0 for (1,3,t). The p=0 instances therefore cannot tell the main evidenced error apart from correct work by final answer.
findings.repair: Add a sample row with credit and feedback for p(OA-OB). Make a:A1 explicitly depend on a correct resultant ('www'). Tag the 6 p=0 and 3 identity tuples as marking fixtures, or exclude p=0.

findings.expected: a:B1 follows the source B1, which accepts the correctly scaled vector minus OB, '(-3p,4p,2p) - (3,-1,2)', or the combined resultant.
findings.actual: a:B1 requires the combined (p-s, rp-1, p+1) or a scalar-product expansion. The report says most candidates reached only the set-up stage, so the narrower wording could withhold the B1 the source gives.
findings.repair: Accept (p, rp, p) - (s, 1, -1) (correct scaling shown with OB subtracted) for a:B1.

findings.expected: Under the template's marking field, the memo states its intermediate-rounding rule and lists rounding-sensitive instances, consistent with NSSCAS 'round only the final answer' (2021 report PDF236; 2025 PDF355).
findings.actual: No intermediate-rounding rule is stated for b:A1. Rounding |OA|, |OB| or cos theta to 3 s.f. (the syllabus default for non-exact answers) changes the 1-dp angle in 5/18 (r,s) pairs, i.e. 15/54 tuples, including both the Normal (61.9 becomes 61.8) and Changed (104.3 becomes 104.2) exemplars. theta(2,-3)=104.25176 is 0.0018 deg from a boundary, so a memo that rounds to 2 dp first and then half-even gives 104.2.
findings.repair: State that b:A1 needs the correctly rounded value and that M marks survive premature rounding. Add a premature-rounding feedback sample. Freeze these 15 tuples as stage E/F fixtures and compute the memo with exact or decimal rounding.

findings.actual: The part (a) reference has learner_display:false but learner_display_reason 'Owner-authorised attributed examination original; source disposition still controls use.', which was copied from the displayable (b) reference.

findings.expected: The subject binding records the native NSSCAS general method/answer-only convention and requires each memo to justify any departure. The playbook forbids a universal penalty but asks for evidence or a stated proposal.
findings.actual: subject-rules.md never mentions it, although marking-conventions.json classes CONVENTION:002 and :076 as 'explicit general rule'. The 2021 report PDF236/printed234 says 'Complete methods should be shown at all times ... No marks are awarded if only answers are given'; 2025 PDF355/printed353 says 'the emphasis in AS is more on the method'. The work orders diverge without reference to it: principal-inverse gives a bare exact x 2/2 'by implied method', citing Cambridge; modulus gives a bare formula 3/3 (consistent with its B1 table); vector gives a bare p 0/3.
findings.repair: Add the general convention with locators to subject-rules. Require each work order's answer-only rule to say whether it follows or departs from it and why. Re-examine the principal-inverse full answer-only credit against the NSSCAS rule.

findings.expected: A misread rule bound for runtime marking (2025 report PDF345/printed343 item 4: 'Learners who misread numbers do not score maximum marks even if their method is correct'; CONVENTION:108).
findings.actual: There is no misread rule in subject-rules, the contract or the vector work order, although the vector design names 'reliable signed-component reading' as its main risk.
findings.repair: Add a proposed misread rule (for example, method marks kept on misread data, accuracy marks lost, never full marks), with a vector sample for a mis-copied sign.

findings.expected: An exactness rule that says what happens when exactness is not requested but the value is exact. Syllabus note 3: 3 s.f. 'if the answer is not exact'; the 2021 and 2025 reports advise exact 'where possible'.
findings.actual: subject-rules says exact forms 'remain exact where requested' and does not say whether a 3 s.f. decimal of an exact rational or surd is accepted when exactness is not requested. This gap produces vector-contract-01.
findings.repair: State the rule explicitly (for example, the exact value or a correct 3 s.f. decimal earns A unless the task says 'exact'), and apply it across work orders.

findings.expected: A runtime policy for multiple or uncancelled answers. 2025 PDF345 item 1 says the first answer seen is marked; CONVENTION:017 defers app response selection to the PLAN.
findings.actual: Neither the PLAN, the contract nor subject-rules decides it; only 'ambiguous' clarification is covered.
findings.repair: Decide (for example, request clarification, or mark the first) and record it as proposed.

findings.expected: Stable, consistent selection IDs. The contract wants 'selection IDs from the accepted analysis' and per-part direct and prerequisite IDs, with classification version, in each work order.
findings.actual: Design selection IDs use three schemes: 8227:SELECT:D:* (visual), 8227:SEL-D:* (calculus), 8227:D:SEL:* (trig/model). The three calculus WOs (implicit-normal, stationary-inflexion, motion-integration) do not name their accepted 8227:FAMILY:* selections, and they defer per-part demand IDs to planning/calculus-design.json. Stationary-inflexion has no prerequisite statement in the WO; the JSON has M1:T8:O01:D02. Six WOs omit the classification version string 8227-pilot-design-0.1.0. Every other required field (purpose, sources/award locators, domains, difficulty bounds, capacity, assets, solution, criteria, answer-only, alternatives, no double credit, samples/feedback, practice/test reveal, checks, seeds, uncertainty) is present in all nine.
findings.evidence: Regex scan plus manual confirmation of every miss.
findings.repair: Normalise the ID scheme. In each WO, list the accepted selection IDs and per-part direct and prerequisite IDs, or a per-part pointer, plus the classification version.

findings.expected: Acceptance tests cover learner input and rendering of column vectors, signed components and degree marks, which the vector design lists as a capability requirement.
findings.actual: APP8227-01 to 08 have no notation input/render item. It is covered only generically by Q10 and the 'response formats' line in local acceptance.
findings.repair: Add a vector/LaTeX input-render acceptance check (entering the resultant for a:B1, minus signs, degree sign, saved history).

findings.expected: One consistent statement of what gates stage E.
findings.actual: The vector WO says its method-dependency proposals need independent review 'before authoring'. PLAN and OWNER-CHECKPOINT gate stage E on owner approval only. This is consistent with playbook D, which needs only owner approval, but unclear about whether these step-3 design-review findings must be dispositioned first.
findings.repair: State in OWNER-CHECKPOINT that the step-3 design-review findings are dispositioned before stage E authoring of affected recipes.

findings.expected: The Q15 copied-wording override cites its authority.
findings.actual: It says 'The user authorises ...' without the decision locator (owner-decisions-2026-11-16.md N2.5, which permits verbatim NSSCAS/Cambridge with attribution). Generated variants still fall under Q15; the vector (b) prompt reuses the whole 7-word source sentence, which is acceptable as command terminology.
findings.repair: Cite N2.5 and keep Q15 for generated variants.
